conventions.convention: AC and the Brownian Ito-process conventions are assumed: usual filtration, adapted vector Brownian motion, and future increments independent of the current filtration.
I_ij integrates the increment of Brownian coordinate i against coordinate j; L_i f = Df sigma_i; A_ij = (I_ij - I_ji)/2. Commutativity means L_i sigma_j = L_j sigma_i everywhere.
C_b^k includes boundedness and continuity of the function itself and all componentwise partial derivatives through order k.
The strong error is max_n E|Y_n-X_tn|², rather than E max_n |Y_n-X_tn|²; the uniform grid has h=T/N≤1 and Y_0=X_0∈L².
Stochastic Heun is scalar with constant additive diffusion, and its predictor and corrector use the same Brownian increment.

The weak-order theorem assumes a bounded classical backward solution with all mixed derivatives indexed by 0≤r≤3 and 0≤j≤6 continuous and bounded; it does not establish that regularity for arbitrary payoffs.
MLMC uses dyadic meshes h_l=T2^(-l), nested fine/coarse Brownian increments, Lipschitz terminal payoffs, fixed finite dimensions, and bounded-cost coefficient and derivative evaluations.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated C_b^3 autonomous SDE and deterministic interval with 0<h≤1, the exact increment equals its general Milstein Taylor increment plus R_t,h∈L², with |E[R_t,h|F_t]|≤Ch² and E[|R_t,h|²|F_t]≤Ch³ almost surely, uniformly in t,h and X_t.

Under its adapted recurrence, Lipschitz drift bound, O(h²) local mean bound, orthogonality conditions, and second-moment bounds E|M|²≤C_1h E|e_n|² and E|Q|²≤C_1h³, e_0=0 and Nh≤T imply E|e_N|²≤C_T h².
Under AC, the stated Brownian filtration, C_b^3 coefficients, commutative noise, X_0∈L² and Y_0=X_0, product-increment Milstein on h=T/N≤1 satisfies max_{0≤n≤N} E|Y_n-X_tn|²≤C_T h².
For deterministic t≥0, h>0, A∈F_t and a finite-energy predictable H supported on (t,t+h], E[1_A|∫H dW^j|²]=E[1_A∫|H|² ds].
For the stated C_b^3 SDE, every t≥0, 0≤r≤1 and A∈F_t satisfy E[1_A|X_t+r-X_t|²]≤Cr P(A) and E[1_A|X_t+r-X_t|⁴]≤Cr² P(A), with uniform coefficient-dependent constants.

I_ij,n+I_ji,n=ΔW_n^i ΔW_n^j−δ_ij h. In the scalar case I_n=((ΔW_n)²−h)/2, with conditional mean zero, conditional second moment h²/2 and conditional covariance with ΔW_n equal to zero. Commutativity gives the stated product-increment reduction.
Under its C_b^6 drift, constant diffusion and bounded backward-solution derivative assumptions, one Heun step from any fixed state x satisfies |E[u(t+h,x+D)]−u(t,x)|≤Ch³ uniformly in t,x,h.

published_dependencies.used_for: Declared choice assumptions inherited from Brownian, Ito and conditional-expectation interfaces.
Usual-filtration conventions, Brownian independence, adapted SDE decomposition and stopping closure.
Filtration nesting in the event-weighted isometry proof.
Discrete filtration convention in the local-to-global lemma.
Elementary predictable approximants and their coefficient measurability.
Finite-sum integral and event-multiplier identity.
Finite-energy iterated integrals and L² approximation by elementary integrands.
Isometry, linearity, finite-energy bounds and approximation limits.
Zero conditional means of finite-energy stochastic integral increments.
Brownian product identity, stopped fourth-moment estimate, coefficient Taylor expansion and geometric Brownian solution verification.
Event-integral characterization of conditional moments and conditional means.
Existence of conditional expectations in the local-defect lemma.
Conditional-expectation linearity, order and contraction properties.
Positive residual variance proving that endpoint increments do not determine I_12.
Gaussian density, scaling, moment calculations and conditional Gaussian computations.
Removing the stopping bound in the fourth-moment estimate.
L² triangle and L¹ bounds in the MLMC and noncommuting-noise arguments.
Coupling marginals, level-zero correction and independent level sample blocks.
Variance and MSE decomposition used by the published complexity theorem.
O(ε^(-2)) work after proving bias exponent α=1, correction-variance exponent β=2 and O(h^(-1)) sample work.

concerns.concern: The title says “Milstein MLMC correction variance and epsilon-squared cost”, whereas the Statement and Proof establish work O(ε^(-2)). The title should say inverse-epsilon-squared cost to match the proved exponent.
